Volumetric audio

Stable Audio Last updated: 2026-11-22

An optional mixer that simulates how sound travels through the world: it arrives late, is Doppler shifted, is muffled by what lies in its way, bends round corners, echoes and rings with the room, and clears up as you get close.

VolumetricMixer (src/caffeine/audio/volumetric/) is separate from AudioService: a game that wants plain 2D or 3D sound keeps using that. The mixer needs no sound card. It renders blocks of stereo samples, so the same code feeds a device in play, a WAV file in a test and a video in the demos.

1. What a voice goes through#

Stage What it does
Propagation The clip is read at t - distance / c, so a shot 150 m away is heard 0.44 s late. A moving source changes that delay continuously, which is the Doppler shift: exact, with no pitch trick (dopplerScale 0 freezes it)
Distance Inverse law gain (half for every doubling) and air absorption: the cutoff falls with distance, so near sound is clear and far sound is dull
Occlusion The segment source to listener is traced through the AcousticWorld. What a wall lets through is quiet and dull: lows pass walls far better than highs, and thicker walls keep less
Diffraction If the sound can bend round the obstacle (the end of a wall, a doorway) that path is mixed in too, quieter and duller with the extra distance, and the voice is heard coming from the opening
The room 31 rays round the listener (up to 300 m) give its size, openness, sky exposure and reflectivity. A feedback delay network (8 lines) fits the reverb tail and level to them, and far hard surfaces send back distinct echoes at 2 d / c. A source behind a wall is in another room: that room is read too, and its own reverb leaks through the wall
Clarity The reverb falls slower than the direct sound, so distant sound is washier and near sound is dry and clear. What reaches the room from behind a wall is only what the wall lets through
Ears A spherical head (8.75 cm): Woodworth's time difference (up to 0.66 ms) and Brown & Duda's head shadow, a filter that boosts the highs in the ear facing the sound and cuts them deeply in the far ear (the lows reach both), and a duller rear. No HRTF data files
Layers World is spatial; Ambient (rain, wind) covers the scene and follows the listener's exposure, muffled and quieter under a roof; Music and Ui are plain. Each layer has its own volume

2. Using it#

cpp
AcousticBoxWorld world;                       // or your own AcousticWorld over the game's colliders
world.add({-500, -1, -500}, {500, 0, 500}, AcousticMaterial::ground(), false);
world.addRoom({-8, 0, -6}, {8, 3, 6}, AcousticMaterial::brick(), 0.3f, /*door*/ 2.0f);

VolumetricMixer mixer(48000);
mixer.setWorld(&world);
mixer.setListener(camera.position, camera.forward);
VoiceId siren = mixer.play({.clip = clip, .position = start, .loop = true});
// each audio block (about 5 ms): move things, then mix
mixer.setPosition(siren, vehicle.position);
mixer.render(stereo, 256);

Move voices and the listener between blocks, with small blocks: the Doppler shift is the change of delay from one block to the next. debug(voice) reports what the mixer decided (distance, delay, pitch ratio, gain, cutoff, blocked, diffracted, where the sound seems to come from), and room() what the rays read. settings() switches each stage off (occlusion, diffraction, reverb, airAbsorption, propagationDelay, ears).

3. The world sound travels through#

AcousticWorld answers two questions: the transmission between two points, and how far a ray goes before it hits something. AcousticBoxWorld is a set of boxes, axis-aligned or oriented (centre, half extents, three axes: a cube entity scaled and turned into a wall), with materials (concrete, brick, wood, glass, foliage, curtain, ground), and addRoom for four walls, a ceiling and an optional doorway. A material says how much of the lows and the highs pass 20 cm of it and how much energy it reflects. A game with other shapes implements the interface over its own colliders.

4. In the editor and in a scene#

The scene decides what is heard, with three reflected components (the Inspector and scripts edit them like any other):

Component What it does
Volumetric Audio The settings: on, the layer and master volumes, the Doppler scale, the speed of sound, and a switch for each stage of section 1. Nothing is mixed without an enabled one
Audio Emitter A sound: Clip Path (a WAV, looked for as written, then under the asset root), Volume, Loop, Play On Spawn, Max Distance, and the new Layer (0 World, 1 Ambient, 2 Music, 3 Ui), Ref Distance and Doppler
Acoustic Obstacle The entity's transform applied to a unit cube is a box sound cannot cross: a preset material (Material) or a custom one (Custom, Transmission Low/High, Reflectivity)

Weather is played by the same mixer when a scene has both: the rain and wind beds are Ambient voices (muffled and quieter under a roof) and every thunder clap is a World voice up in the sky at its bearing, so a wall muffles it, a hall rings with it and the ears place it. Weather > Audio Enabled and Audio Volume switch it on, as before; the clap is not delayed twice (propagate off on that voice, because the strike's own clock already waited out the travel time).

SceneAudio reads them once a frame, builds a new box world only when the obstacles changed, and gives voices and the listener a velocity from the time between frames, so the mixer carries them on smoothly and the Doppler shift stays continuous at any frame rate. The viewport camera is the listener. VolumetricAudio owns the mixer, a lock and the optional sound device (the system default or one of outputDevices(), listed in a stable order), which pulls blocks on the audio thread; with no device the session mixes silently ("monitors"), so the numbers keep moving and tests can pull samples with caffeine_session_volumetric_render. C ABI v20 adds caffeine_session_volumetric_state, caffeine_session_volumetric_voice, caffeine_session_set_audio_output, caffeine_session_set_audio_output_device, caffeine_audio_output_device_count/_name and caffeine_session_volumetric_render.

Doppio's Audio tab (View menu, with Inspector, Profiler, Photon and Environment) adds the component, edits it with undo, switches the speakers on and off, picks the sound device, adds a source or a 6 x 3 x 0.3 m wall, and shows live what the mixer decides: the room round the listener and one line per sound (distance, level, low-pass, pitch shift, behind a wall or round a corner). Agents use show_audio, audio, audio_add, audio_set, audio_output, audio_device, audio_add_source and audio_add_wall.

caffeine-runtime hosts it too: each frame it syncs the scene from the active Camera 3D, feeds the weather from its renderer, and opens the sound device the first frame the scene has a Volumetric Audio component.

5. Hear it#

scripts/render-audio-demo.py renders four scenarios with sounds from references/moodist and writes videos to build/audio-demo/videos/ (a top view of the scene with what the mixer is doing, and the audio):

Video What to listen for
doppler.mp4 An ambulance at 108 km/h with Doppler on and off, then an aeroplane at 150 m/s
shots.mp4 A shot 150 m away in a field with a far cliff (late, dull, echoed), the same shot in a concrete hall, and from outside its wall
occlusion.mp4 A radio behind a wall, then round its end; a fan inside a house, then at its door
layers.mp4 Rain and wind outside and in a house, a fireplace you walk up to, thunder through the walls, and the ambient layer at 30%

It needs cmake --build build --target caffeine-audio-demo, ffmpeg, Pillow and numpy.

6. Tests and limits#

  • tests/test_scene_audio.cpp: emitters become voices, an obstacle blocks them, moving and removing, no component means silence, and the weather through the mixer (beds follow it, a roof muffles them, a clap comes from its side of the sky). tests/test_volumetric_audio.cpp: level halves with distance, the delay is d / c, the Doppler shift matches 1 / (1 -+ v / c) within 2%, near sound is brighter, a wall takes at least 15 dB and the highs more than the lows, a thicker wall takes more, a short wall is bent round and heard from its corner, the rays read open and shut rooms and far echoes, a shot rings in a hall and echoes off a cliff, the ears, the ambient layer indoors and layer volumes, and the limiter.
  • Geometry is boxes (oriented ones from a scene); triangle meshes are not traced. The acoustics are a model, not a wave solver: occlusion is one traced segment plus one best detour, the listener's room and the room of a source behind a wall are each fitted by their own rays and shared reverb, and echoes come from the listener's rays.
  • The mixer is mono per voice, and the ears are a model of a spherical head, not measured HRTF data: left and right are good, front and back and up and down are only suggested (a dull rear). Nothing else changes: a scene without the component sounds as before.
